mainTopic: Birth days counting toward a זבה's clean days, and the impurity of דם הנדה whether moist or dry
overview: The amud opens with a question: a זבה gives birth, and she sees no blood during the days of impurity after the birth. Do those days count toward her seven clean days for זיבה? רב כהנא brings a ברייתא about a woman who miscarried something unknown, which says those days do count. רב פפא tries to reject the proof, but רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע shows the rejection fails, and the גמרא concludes that the days count. The ברייתא then works out how many days a woman with a fixed cycle of bleeding and clean days may be with her husband. Then the chapter בא סימן ends, and a new chapter opens with a משנה. The משנה teaches that דם הנדה and בשר המת make things impure even when dry, while other substances stay impure only while moist, unless they can be soaked back to their original form. The גמרא finds verses for the impurity of דם הנדה, including dry blood. It then explains, from the word ״היא״, that her blood does not make a מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב impure.

steps.title: Do blood-free birth days count toward a זבה's clean days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the days of impurity after a birth, on which the woman sees no blood, count toward her seven clean days from זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The days after birth on which she does not see blood: do they count toward the counting of her זיבה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. A woman who is a זבה gave birth, and we want to know whether her blood-free days after the birth count as clean days for her זיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זבה must count seven days with no blood before she can become pure. After a birth, a woman is impure from לידה for a set time even without bleeding. Those days have no blood, but she is still impure for a different reason, so it is unclear whether they can serve as 'clean' days for זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of impurity after giving birth (seven for a boy, fourteen for a girl)
What is the law? (opens a question)
The counting of seven clean days a זבה needs to become pure
That they should count toward (literally, 'go up')

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether she is impure during the birth days. She definitely is. The question is only whether those same days can also count toward finishing her זיבה.

phrases.english: The days of birth on which she does not see blood
phrases.notes: This is a woman who was already a זבה when she gave birth.

phrases.english: what is the law: do they count toward the counting of her זיבה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether blood-free days of לידה impurity count as clean days toward the seven clean days of זיבה.

steps.title: A woman saw blood two days and miscarried on the third
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא brings a ברייתא about a woman who saw blood for two days, miscarried on the third, and does not know what she miscarried. She is in doubt whether she is a זבה or a woman who gave birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Come and hear. A woman saw blood two days, and on the third day she miscarried, and she does not know what she miscarried. This is a case of doubt: maybe זיבה, maybe לידה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא starts bringing a proof from a ברייתא. This step lays out the case; the part that answers our question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two days of blood are not yet enough to make her a full זבה. Whether she becomes one depends on what happened on the third day. Since she does not know whether she miscarried a real baby, or whether there was blood, she is in doubt about both זיבה and לידה.

keyTerms.meaning: She miscarried
In doubt whether she is a זבה
In doubt whether she gave birth

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: Come and hear,
she saw blood two days, and on the third she miscarried,
and she does not know what she miscarried —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זוֹ סְפֵק זִיבָה, סְפֵק לֵידָה.
phrases.english: this woman is in doubt of זיבה and in doubt of birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to answer the question of step 1.
steps.raayaObject: Whether blood-free birth days count toward the seven clean days of זיבה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a woman who saw blood two days and miscarried an unknown object on the third.

steps.title: Her blood-free birth days count toward her זיבה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that she brings a קרבן that is not eaten, and her blood-free birth days count toward her זיבה count. This answers the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: She brings an offering, but it is not eaten. And the days of her birth on which she does not see blood count for her toward the counting of her זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line of the ברייתא that answers the question. It says outright that birth days without blood count toward her זיבה count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the doubt, she must bring a קרבן, but the כהנים cannot eat it since we don't know what kind of offering it is, or whether she needed one at all. The last line is the proof: days that are impure because of לידה but have no blood still count as clean days for זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought to the בית המקדש
And it is not eaten (because its status is in doubt)
They count for her

steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא, days of לידה impurity with no blood DO count toward a זבה's seven clean days.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being impure for one reason (birth) does not stop the days from counting as clean for another reason (זיבה). What matters for the count is that no blood was seen.

phrases.english: she brings an offering, and it is not eaten,
and the days of her birth on which she does not see blood —
count for her toward the counting of her זיבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וִימֵי לֵידָתָהּ שֶׁאֵין רוֹאָה בָּהֶן עוֹלִין לָהּ לִסְפִירַת זִיבָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 2 and gives the ruling that answers step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Blood-free days of לידה impurity count toward the seven clean days of זיבה.

steps.title: רב פפא rejects the proof: the extra days may not be birth days at all
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues the ברייתא proves nothing, because the extra seven days count only on the chance that she gave birth to a boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: That case is different. It is possible she gave birth to a boy. That is why all those extra seven days we give her count toward her זיבה count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא is pushing back on the proof from the ברייתא. He says it does not really answer our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she had a girl, she is impure for fourteen days. If she had a boy, only seven. The second set of seven days is kept strict only in case it was a girl. If it was really a boy, those days are not birth days at all, so of course they count. So the ברייתא says nothing about days that are surely birth days.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; that case does not prove our point
A woman who gave birth to a boy (seven days of impurity)
Extra (the additional seven days)
The count of seven clean days a זבה needs

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying birth days never count. He only says this ברייתא cannot prove that they do.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is different there,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר יוֹלֶדֶת זָכָר הִיא,
phrases.english: since one can say she is a woman who gave birth to a male,
phrases.notes: After a boy she is impure for only seven days, not fourteen.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל הָנֵי שִׁבְעָה יַתִּירֵי דְּקָיָהֲבִינַן לַהּ
phrases.english: and all these extra seven days that we give her
count for her toward the counting of her זיבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 2-3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא, so for now the question of step 1 is unproven. Step 5 then challenges this rejection, and step 6 accepts the proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra seven days may not be birth days at all (if it was a boy), so they cannot show that real birth days count.

steps.title: רב הונא challenges רב פפא: she might also have had a girl
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע points out that a girl is just as possible as a boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said to רב פפא: Do we only consider that she might have had a boy, and not that she might have had a girl?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא challenges רב פפא's rejection with a question that makes a point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both options are equally possible. If birth days did not count, we would have to worry that it was a girl and not count those days. Yet the ברייתא still counts them. That attacks רב פפא's escape.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who gave birth to a girl (fourteen days of impurity)
To be in doubt; to take a possibility into account

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rav Pappa:
Regarding a woman who gave birth to a male there is room for doubt,
but regarding a woman who gave birth to a female there is no room for doubt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's rejection in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the days count only because she may have had a boy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The doubt goes both ways. The days still count even though it may have been a girl, when they would be real birth days.

steps.title: Conclusion: birth days do count toward the זיבה count
steps.stepSummary: The proof stands: blood-free birth days count toward her seven clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: So isn't the lesson that they count? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע finishes his challenge: the ברייתא must mean the days count. The גמרא then agrees with 'שמע מינה'. The days do count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב פפא's escape failed, the ברייתא again proves the point. The repeated 'שמע מינה' is the גמרא saying yes, that is right. This answers the question from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that...
They count (literally, they go up toward the count)
Learn from it; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: Days of impurity after birth on which she sees no blood DO count toward a זבה's seven clean days.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so: learn from it that they count,
learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ עוֹלִין, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion that follows from step 5's challenge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Blood-free birth-impurity days count toward the seven clean days of זיבה.

steps.title: Nine days of bleeding and nine clean days: eight permitted days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a woman with a fixed cycle of nine bleeding days and nine clean days may be with her husband on eight days out of eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she bleeds nine days and is clean nine days, she may be with her husband on eight days out of the eighteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to finish quoting the ברייתא, which now gives cases of fixed bleeding cycles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first seven days of bleeding are her נדה days. Days eight and nine are זיבה days. Bleeding on only one or two days means she waits one clean day, which is day ten. That leaves days eleven to eighteen, which is eight days.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure days, meaning days she sees blood
Pure days, meaning days without blood
She may be with her husband

phrases.english: Nine days impure,
phrases.notes: This means a fixed pattern: she sees blood for nine days in a row, then repeats.

phrases.english: and nine days pure —

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת שְׁמוֹנָה יָמִים מִתּוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר.
phrases.english: she may engage in intercourse eight days out of eighteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּשְׁעָה יָמִים טְמֵאִין, וְתִשְׁעָה יָמִים טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion and goes back to quoting the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cycle of 9 bleeding and 9 clean days: 7 נדה days, 2 זיבה days, 1 clean day of waiting, then 8 permitted days.

steps.title: Ten and ten: her permitted days equal her זיבה days
steps.stepSummary: With ten bleeding and ten clean days, the number of permitted days equals the number of זיבה days, and this holds for any larger equal cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she bleeds ten days and is clean ten days, her permitted days are the same in number as her זיבה days. The same is true for a hundred, and the same for a thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second cycle and then turns it into a general pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven days are נדה, then three days are זיבה, which makes her a full זבה. She must count seven clean days, which leaves three permitted days, the same as her three זיבה days. With a hundred and a hundred, it is ninety-three זיבה days and ninety-three permitted days, and so on.

keyTerms.meaning: The days she may be with her husband
The days she sees זיבה blood
A woman who saw blood three days in a row outside her נדה time, and needs seven clean days

steps.whatToRemember: In an equal cycle of three or more זיבה days, the seven נדה days at the start and the seven clean days at the end cancel out. So permitted days equal זיבה days.

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים טְמֵאִין וַעֲשָׂרָה יָמִים טְהוֹרִים —
phrases.english: Ten days impure and ten days pure —
the days she may engage in intercourse are like the days of her זיבה,
phrases.notes: That is three and three: days 8-10 are זיבה, days 11-17 are clean days, and days 18-20 are permitted.

phrases.english: and so too for a hundred, and so too for a thousand.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים טְמֵאִין וַעֲשָׂרָה יָמִים טְהוֹרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the next cycle and turns it into a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In equal cycles of ten or more, permitted days equal זיבה days.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק בא סימן
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the chapter בא סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter בא סימן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is formally finishing the chapter called בא סימן. A brand-new chapter starts right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional goodbye to a chapter we have learned, with a promise to come back to it. It contains no new הלכה. It only marks a boundary between chapters.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula said when finishing a chapter
The name of the chapter now being completed

phrases.english: We will return to you, [chapter] 'בא סימן'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter whose last discussion was the counting of a woman's fixed cycles in step 8.

steps.title: Menstrual blood and corpse flesh are impure whether moist or dry
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens: דם הנדה and בשר המת make things impure both when moist and when dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: The blood of a נדה and the flesh of a dead person make things impure when they are moist, and also when they are dry.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. It names two substances that stay impure even after they dry out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most impure liquids or soft substances lose their power once they dry up. The משנה starts with two strong exceptions: דם הנדה and בשר המת keep their impurity even when completely dry.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood of a menstruating woman
The flesh of a dead body
Moist, wet
Dry
They make things impure

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole chapter's question: does a substance's impurity depend on it still being moist?

phrases.english: MISHNA: The blood of a menstruating woman,
and the flesh of a dead body —
make impure when moist, and make impure when dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דם הנדה and בשר המת make things impure whether moist or dry.

steps.title: Other impure substances make things impure only while moist
steps.stepSummary: זוב, mucus, spit, שרץ, נבלה and שכבת זרע make things impure when moist, but not when dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the זוב discharge, mucus, spit, a creeping animal, an animal carcass and semen make things impure only when moist. When they are dry, they do not make things impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now contrasts the first two substances with a list of others. These others lose their impurity once they dry out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבל signals a contrast with step 10. For this second group, being moist is the condition for impurity. Once dry, they are no longer treated as impure substances.

keyTerms.meaning: The discharge of a זב
Mucus
Saliva, spit
A creeping animal whose carcass is impure
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Semen

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two lists. Only דם הנדה and בשר המת stay impure when dry. Everything in this second list does not, unless it can be soaked back, which comes in the next step.

phrases.english: But the discharge of a זב, and the mucus, and the saliva,
and the creeping animal, and the animal carcass,
and semen —
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, but the corrected wording is the one in square brackets.

phrases.english: make impure when moist, but do not make impure when dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts a second group of substances with the two in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זוב, mucus, spit, שרץ, נבלה and שכבת זרע make things impure only when moist.

steps.title: If they can be soaked back to their original state, they stay impure even when dry
steps.stepSummary: Substances from the second list that can be soaked and restored make things impure even when dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if these dry substances can be soaked and go back to the way they were, they make things impure when moist and also when dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an exception to the rule of step 11. A dry substance that can be restored by soaking is still treated as impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dryness only removes impurity if the substance is truly 'gone' from its old form. If soaking can bring it back to what it was, it is still considered the same impure substance, even while it sits dry.

keyTerms.meaning: To be soaked (in liquid)
To go back to how they were

phrases.english: And if they can be soaked
and return to how they were —
they make impure when moist and make impure when dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 11 with an exception for restorable substances.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dry substance from the second list that can be soaked back to its original state still makes things impure.

steps.title: How long must the soaking last?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what soaking test decides whether a substance can be restored.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much soaking do they need?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a clarifying question about step 12. It is setting up the answer that comes right next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 depends on whether a substance 'can be soaked back.' This question asks for a clear test, so we know what kind of soaking counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Their soaking

phrases.english: And how much is their soaking?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure of the soaking mentioned in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length and conditions of the soaking test.

steps.title: In lukewarm water for a full day
steps.stepSummary: The test is soaking in lukewarm water for twenty-four hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: In lukewarm water, for a full twenty-four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question. The soaking test is lukewarm water for one full day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the exception in step 12 has a clear measure. If a dry substance returns to its original state after a day in lukewarm water, it counts as still impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Lukewarm water
From one moment to the same moment the next day: a full 24 hours

phrases.english: In lukewarm water for twenty-four hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Soaking in lukewarm water for 24 hours.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: dry corpse flesh that cannot be restored is pure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says dry בשר המת that cannot be soaked back to its original state is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: flesh of a dead person that is dry and cannot be soaked back to how it was is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds his own view about בשר המת. He applies the soaking test to it as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 listed בשר המת with no limit, as impure even when dry. רבי יוסי adds a condition: if it is so dried out that soaking cannot restore it, it is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure, not carrying impurity
Dry

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not saying all dry corpse flesh is pure. He means only flesh that is so dried out that soaking cannot restore it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Flesh of a dead body that is dry,
and cannot be soaked
and return to how it was — is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the soaking test of steps 12–14 to בשר המת, which step 10 had listed without that condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dry בשר המת that cannot be restored by soaking is טהור.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule about דם הנדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Where do we learn these things from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for the source of the משנה's first rule. It is setting up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in the next step shows that the question is aimed at the impurity of דם הנדה. Before discussing why it stays impure when dry, the גמרא first wants a source that the blood carries impurity at all.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned? A request for a source

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא and asks for the source of step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source that דם הנדה makes things impure.

steps.title: חזקיה: the flow is compared to the woman herself
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה learns from 'והדוה בנדתה' that the menstrual flow is impure just like the נדה herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: the פסוק says 'and her who is unwell in her נדה state.' Her flow is like her. Just as she makes things impure, her flow also makes things impure.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the question with a פסוק. He reads it as comparing the woman's flow to the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הדוה, 'the one who is unwell,' is read as connected to מדוה, 'her flow.' Since the פסוק places the woman and her condition together, her flow takes on her status. Just as a נדה makes things impure, so does her blood.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And her who is unwell in her נדה state' (ויקרא 15:33)
Her flow: the menstrual blood
Like her
Just as ... so too: a comparison formula

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the basic source that דם הנדה is impure. The question of why dry blood is impure comes next.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said:
As the verse says: 'And her who is unwell in her menstrual state' —
her flow is like her,
just as she makes impure,
so too her flow makes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'והדוה בנדתה' compares the flow to the woman, so the blood is impure just as she is.

steps.title: We have a source for moist blood, but what about dry blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that חזקיה's verse covers moist blood and asks for a source that dry blood is also טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source that moist blood is impure. How do we know dry blood is impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says חזקיה's source works for moist blood. Now it asks where we learn that dried-out blood is also impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing the blood to the נדה herself (״והדוה בנדתה״) clearly fits fresh, flowing blood. Dry blood looks like a different thing, so the גמרא wants a separate source for it. This connects to the משנה's rule that dry דם הנדה is still טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Moist, fresh (here: liquid blood)
Dry (here: dried-out blood)
From where do we know it? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: We have found [a source for] moist [blood];
phrases.notes: He means חזקיה's verse from the step before, ״והדוה בנדתה״.

phrases.english: dry [blood], from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows חזקיה's derivation to moist blood and asks for a source for dry blood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that dry דם הנדה is impure.

steps.title: רבי יצחק learns from ״יהיה״ that the blood keeps its status
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says the word ״יהיה״ teaches that the blood stays in its impure state even after it dries.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: the verse says ״יהיה״ (it shall be). That means it stays as it was.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question. The word ״יהיה״ in the פסוק teaches that the blood keeps its status, so it stays impure even when it dries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״יהיה״ means 'it shall be,' and רבי יצחק reads it as 'it stays the way it was.' Blood that was impure while moist does not lose that טומאה when it dries. Notice this reading speaks about blood that changed from moist to dry, which the next step will pick up on.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall remain in its existing state

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
The verse says: "shall be"
in its existing state it shall be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״יהיה״ teaches that the blood keeps its impure status even when dry.

steps.title: That only covers blood that dried later, not blood dry from the start or the dissolving test
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on two points. רבי יצחק's reading only covers blood that was moist and then dried. It does not explain the משנה about a woman who discharges red bits that dissolve in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you could say this only applies to blood that was moist and then became dry. How do we know about blood that was dry from the beginning? And also, the משנה teaches that if a woman discharges something like a shell, soil, a hair, or red mosquitoes, she puts it in water, and if it dissolves she is impure. How do we know that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's reading. 'It stays as it was' only fits blood that started moist, so it leaves two cases without a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״יהיה״ means 'stays in its state,' it needs a moist starting point to stay in. That leaves no source for blood that came out already dry. It also leaves no source for the משנה's case of hard red pieces that turn out to be blood when they dissolve.

keyTerms.meaning: Dry from the very start
And furthermore (adding a second challenge)
A woman who discharges (something from her body)
Small flying insects, like mosquitoes
They dissolved

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether dry blood is impure. Everyone agrees it is. The question is only which source proves it, since 'stays as it was' seems to fit only blood that began moist.

phrases.english: But say: these words apply
to [blood that was] moist and became dry;
[blood] dry from the start, from where do we know?
And furthermore, that which we learned [in a משנה]:
A woman who discharges something like a shell, like soil,
like a hair, like red mosquitoes,
she should throw [them] into water;
if they dissolved, she is impure.
From where do we know [this]?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּלַח וְנַעֲשָׂה יָבֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reach of רבי יצחק's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's reading of ״יהיה״ as 'stays in its state'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Staying' needs a moist starting point, so the reading cannot cover blood that was dry from the start or pieces that only show they are blood by dissolving.

steps.title: ״יהיה״ is an inclusion that covers every form of the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ״יהיה״ is a ריבוי, a word that includes, so it covers blood in all its forms.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״יהיה״ is an inclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. ״יהיה״ is not only about staying the same; it is a word that includes and widens the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading ״יהיה״ as a ריבוי makes the law much broader. Blood that dried later, blood that was dry from the start, and hard red pieces that dissolve in water are all included as טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: An inclusion: a word that widens a law to more cases

steps.whatToRemember: ״יהיה״ is a ריבוי. It makes דם הנדה impure in any form: moist, dried, dry from the start, or in pieces that dissolve.

phrases.english: "Shall be" is an inclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the verse: ״יהיה״ is a general inclusion, not just 'stays in its state'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״יהיה״ only keeps blood impure if it was moist and later dried.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״יהיה״ includes all forms of דם הנדה.

steps.title: If the blood is like her, it should also make a bed and seat impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if her blood is compared to the נדה herself, it should also make a מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב impure, strongly enough to make a person and his clothes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as she makes a bed and a seat impure, so that they make a person impure and make clothes impure, her blood should also make a bed and a seat impure, so that they make a person impure and make clothes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to חזקיה's comparison of the blood to the נדה and pushes it further. If the blood is like her in every way, it should also make a bed or seat impure the way she does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדה who lies or sits on something makes it a מִשְׁכָּב or מוֹשָׁב. Such an item is impure enough to make a person impure, and also the clothes that person is wearing. If the blood is exactly like her, it should have this same strong power.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, just as (setting up a 'same rule' argument)
An item made impure by being lain on or sat on
To make clothes impure (the person's clothes become impure along with him)

phrases.english: If so, just as she
makes [something she lies on as] a bed and [something she sits on as] a seat
to make a person impure and to make clothes impure,

phrases.aramaic: אַף דָּמָהּ נָמֵי עוֹשֶׂה מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב
phrases.english: so too, her blood should also make a bed and a seat
to make a person impure and to make clothes impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה הִיא עוֹשָׂה מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge on חזקיה's comparison of the blood to the נדה.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's comparison of דם הנדה to the נדה herself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the blood is fully like her, it should also have her power to make מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב impure.

steps.title: Blood cannot lie or sit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that blood is not something that can lie or sit, so the laws of מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב do not apply to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is her blood something that can lie or sit?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a sharp rhetorical question. A bed or seat becomes impure only when someone lies or sits on it, and blood cannot do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה of מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב comes from the act of lying or sitting. Blood does not lie or sit, so this kind of טומאה simply does not fit it. The comparison to the נדה still stands; this law just has nothing to apply to.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it as if...? (a rhetorical question meaning 'surely not')
Capable of, belonging to (here: able to lie and sit)

phrases.english: Is it as if her blood
is capable of lying and sitting?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ דָּמָה בַּר מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical limit: the law needs something that can lie or sit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the blood is like her, it makes מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood cannot lie or sit, so מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב does not apply to it.

steps.title: A צרעת stone cannot lie or sit either, yet a verse was needed to exclude it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. An אבן מנוגעת cannot lie or sit, yet a verse was needed to exclude it from מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב. So 'it cannot lie or sit' is not enough on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, can a stone with צרעת lie or sit, that a verse was needed to exclude it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 23. If 'cannot lie or sit' were enough, we would never need a verse to exclude a צרעת stone, which also cannot lie or sit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that a verse was needed to exclude the stone shows that something can make a bed or seat impure without lying or sitting itself. If so, the blood could also make a bed or seat impure, unless a verse excludes it too.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turning someone's logic against him)
A stone of a house that has צרעת
To exclude (from a law)

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
a stone afflicted with צרעת,
is it capable of lying and sitting,
that a verse was needed to exclude it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ, אֶבֶן מְנוּגַּעַת בַּת מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that blood cannot cause מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב because it cannot lie or sit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A צרעת stone also cannot lie or sit, yet the תורה needed a verse to exclude it, so 'cannot lie or sit' does not settle the matter.

steps.title: The ברייתא that considered making a צרעת stone cause מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא behind the challenge. It begins: one might think a צרעת stone makes a bed and seat impure, enough to make a person and clothes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One might think that a stone with צרעת would make a bed and a seat impure, to make a person impure and to make clothes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for its challenge, a ברייתא that seriously considers this law for a צרעת stone. This is the opening line; the ברייתא continues in the next part with its reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'one might think' show that the ברייתא treated it as a real possibility. That proves that being unable to lie or sit does not automatically rule out מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב. This is what gives the challenge in step 24 its force.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introducing an idea the ברייתא will later reject)

phrases.english: As it was taught [in a ברייתא]:
One might think that a stone afflicted with צרעת
would make a bed and a seat [impure],
to make a person impure, to make clothes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא source for the challenge in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That a verse was needed to exclude a צרעת stone from מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that opens with 'one might think' a צרעת stone causes מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב.

steps.title: The ברייתא's קל וחומר: a צרעת stone should make a bed and seat impure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא argues that if a זב, who does not make things impure by entering a house, makes a bed and seat impure, then a צרעת stone, which does make things impure by entering, should certainly make a bed and seat impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is logical: a זב does not make things impure by entering a house, yet he makes a bed and seat impure, strongly enough to make a person and clothes impure. A צרעת stone does make things impure by entering a house. Is it not logical that it should make a bed and seat impure, strongly enough to make a person and clothes impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the ברייתא from Step 25. Here the ברייתא gives its reason for thinking a צרעת stone would make a bed and seat impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא builds a קל וחומר. In one area, impurity by entering a house, the stone is stronger than the זב. So it argues the stone should also match the זב in the area of מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב. The ברייתא is still building up the idea that it will knock down in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is logical. This opens a reasoning argument, here a קל וחומר.
A man with a certain kind of bodily discharge that makes him impure.
Entering. Here it means making things impure just by coming into a house.
A bed and a seat. These are items made for lying or sitting, which can get a strong level of impurity.
A stone of a house that has צרעת.

steps.confusionAlert: This קל וחומר is NOT the final הלכה. The ברייתא raises it only so it can reject it with a verse in the next step.

phrases.english: And it is logical: if a zav,
who does not make impure by entering,
phrases.notes: When a זב walks into a house, the things inside do not become impure just because he came in.

phrases.english: makes a bed and a seat impure
so that it makes a person impure and makes clothes impure,
then a stone with tzara'at, which does make impure by entering,
is it not logical that it makes a bed and a seat impure
so that it makes a person impure and makes clothes impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִין הוּא: וּמָה זָב, שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא בְּבִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quote of the ברייתא begun in Step 25, giving its קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge in Step 24 that 'cannot lie or sit' is not enough to rule out מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that builds a קל וחומר from a זב to a צרעת stone.

steps.title: The ברייתא's conclusion: the word ״הזב״ excludes the stone
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר. The verse says ״הזב״, which teaches that only the זב, and not a צרעת stone, makes a bed and seat impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says ״הזב״: the זב, and not a צרעת stone.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by bringing a verse that blocks the קל וחומר. The word ״הזב״ limits this law to the זב only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word ״הזב״ is read as a limit: this law applies to the זב and to nothing else. So the stone does not make a bed and seat impure. This finishes the ברייתא that the גמרא is using against the answer from Step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the verse says. It brings a verse to decide the question.
A word in a verse that limits or excludes something.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "the zav"
"the zav," and not a stone with tzara'at.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא by rejecting the קל וחומר of Step 26 with a verse.
steps.raayaObject: That a verse was needed to exclude the stone from מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word ״הזב״ in ויקרא 15:4, as read by the ברייתא.

steps.title: The inference: without the verse, the stone would make a bed and seat impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the point from the ברייתא. The only reason the stone is excluded is the verse. Without it, the stone would make a bed and seat impure, even though it cannot lie or sit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that the verse excluded it. But if not for that, it would make impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out why it quoted the ברייתא. This sharpens the challenge from Step 24 against the answer in Step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'a stone cannot lie or sit' were enough, the ברייתא would not need a verse. Since it needed ״הזב״, we see that without a verse even something that cannot lie or sit would make a bed and seat impure. So the reason given in Step 23 for נדה blood no longer works by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason. It points to what alone is causing the ruling.
That the verse excluded it.
But if not for this. It shows what the law would be otherwise.

phrases.english: The reason is that the verse excluded it,
but if not for that, it would make impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּמַעֲטַיהּ קְרָא, הָא לָאו הָכִי מְטַמְּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenging inference out of the ברייתא quoted in Steps 25 to 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 23 that blood cannot lie or sit, so מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב does not apply.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse was needed to exclude the stone, which also cannot lie or sit. So 'cannot lie or sit' alone does not exclude something from מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב.

steps.title: The answer: just as ״הזב״ excludes the stone, ״היא״ excludes her blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the same idea. Just as ״הזב״ excludes the stone, the verse about the נדה says ״אשר היא יושבת עליו״. ״היא״ means she makes a seat impure, and not her blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from this itself comes the answer: didn't you say ״הזב״, and not a צרעת stone? So too the verse says ״אשר היא יושבת עליו״: she, and not her blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the challenge into its answer. It finds a limiting word in the נדה verse that does the same job as ״הזב״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that a verse is needed, not just logic. It finds one: the word ״היא״ (she) limits מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב to the woman herself. So her blood is excluded by a verse, just like the stone.

keyTerms.meaning: And from it. The answer comes from the very source used to ask.
So too. Applying the same pattern to our case.
She, and not her blood. Only the woman herself makes a seat impure.

steps.whatToRemember: נדה blood makes things impure, but it does not make a מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב impure. This is not because blood cannot lie or sit, but because the word ״היא״ in the verse excludes it, just as ״הזב״ excludes a צרעת stone.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the method of this סוגיא: logic alone was not enough to exclude something from מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב. A limiting word in the verse is what does the job.

phrases.english: And from this itself: didn't you say "the zav"
and not a stone with tzara'at?
So too, the verse says:
"upon which she sits"
she, and not her blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִינַּהּ: לָאו מִי אָמְרַתְּ ״הַזָּב״ — וְלֹא אֶבֶן מְנוּגַּעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 28 by using the same kind of verse-based exclusion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a verse to exclude, in place of the logical reason that was rejected.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a verse was needed to exclude the stone, maybe נדה blood, which has no such verse, would make a מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is such a verse: ״אשר היא יושבת עליו״. ״היא״ means she, and not her blood, so the blood does not make a מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב impure.
